messages:
erin: Noticed a persistent 95p+ increase in model-gen tail latency in eu-west this morning. Traces point to r12 hosts showing NIC tx_dropped spikes and heavy L4 egress. Suspect a tenant running bulk dataset-to-GPU transfers over the rack uplink.
matt: Confirmed on synthetic. Hosts 10.5.23.5-10.5.23.9 show tx_dropped rising alongside 99p latency. No recent kernel/driver pushes.
sana: Can someone run `ethtool -S` and `tc -s qdisc` on an affected host and capture a short pcap? Need packet sizes/patterns. Also check ToR counters for VLAN fanout.
erin: Pasted quick outputs from 10.5.23.6:
`ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "tx_packets|tx_bytes|tx_dropped"`
tx_packets: 98765432
tx_bytes: 12345678901
tx_dropped: 2134
`tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` -> shows mq root and intermittent tbf child with 0 bytes sent on some hosts.
kai: Short-term options: 1) apply host-level egress shaping for the tenant IP ranges, 2) steer the tenant's non-prod jobs to our US spare pool, or 3) temporary dedicated carveout (if we can shard a slice). Each has tradeoffs: shaping is fastest; carveout needs billing note.
luca: Note eu-west Dedicated capacity is ~90% used after renewals. We don't have many spare GPUs to reassign without impacting dedicated customers. Carveouts would need finance sign-off if we charge burst premium.
matt: I'll push a conservative `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root tbf rate 1gbit burst 64k latency 200ms` on affected hosts and add `tc filter` to match the tenant's pod CIDR to 500mbit. Will run for 10m and monitor.
sana: Start a 2min pcap on one host: `tcpdump -nn -s 256 -w /tmp/egress-10.5.23.6.pcap host 10.5.23.6 and port not 22` and upload to ops-bucket. Also snapshot ToR VLAN counters and flow stats.
erin: Ops-bot open ticket? We should track cost/billing and tenant comms.
ops-bot: Incident INC-8024 opened, assigned to #eng-infra. Tags: noisy-tenant, egress, billing-potential.
matt: Shaping in progress. Initial result: tx_dropped down ~60%, 95p latency from ~320ms -> ~120ms. Will keep shaping and correlate with pcap.
kai: For medium-term plan: propose eBPF-based per-tenant egress policer on ToRs + control-plane quota enforcement. Low-latency, programmable, but needs ToR agent kernel modules and a 2-sprint rollout with canaries. Advantages: no VLAN sharding, consistent enforcement.
luca: Also recommend policy: any tenant requesting a temporary dedicated carveout pays a burst premium and we auto-bill. Ops finance needs a short write-up.
sana: Important: verify this isn't a driver bug. Shaping masks symptom. If we see anomalous packet retrans patterns or NIC errcounts, escalate to hw team.
erin: I'll ping solutions to tell the tenant we observed extreme egress and asked them to pause bulk transfers for 30m while we investigate. Keep ticket open until pcap + tenant confirmation + plan scheduled.
matt: Update 09:18 UTC: shaping holding; logs uploaded to ops-bucket at s3://ops/INC-8024/pcaps/egress-10.5.23.6.pcap. Monitoring for 15m before closing incident.
erin: Thanks everyone. Action items: (erin) coordinate tenant comms; (matt) keep shaping + collect metrics; (sana) parse pcap and ToR flows; (kai) draft eBPF policer RFC. We'll reconvene if spike reappears. :thumbsup:
